narrative.overview: Medix embodies the atmosphere of a modern, world-class clinic: architectural clarity, quiet clinical authority, and calm reassurance. Visual elements are governed by strict spatial discipline, crisp typography, and restrained surfaces that instill immediate trust in patients managing sensitive healthcare decisions.
keyCharacteristics: Architectural Grid Restraint: Rigorous alignment, generous breathing room, and structured columnar layouts.
Calibrated Semantic Palette: Distinct chromatic lanes for clinical navigation (Clarity Teal), active status/health (Vital Emerald), decisive bookings (Terracotta), and clinical AI (Assist Violet).
Layered Surface Truth: Flat by default with razor-thin hairline borders; elevation is structural, appearing only on floating overlays, sheets, and modal dialogs.
Dignified Data Presentation: Clear tabular structures, explicit appointment lifecycle badges, and high-contrast clinical reports.

rules.name: The Semantic Separation Rule
rules.body: Each chromatic hue holds exclusive ownership over its domain: Teal owns navigation/branding, Emerald owns health/availability, Terracotta owns transactional booking/checkout, and Violet owns clinical AI. They never substitute for one another.

rules.name: The Tint Pair Doctrine
rules.body: Every status badge or contextual pill must pair its solid semantic foreground with its designated 10% tint background. Badges never use raw opacity overlays that muddy text contrast.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Mandate
rules.body: All financial prices (BDT), clinical timestamps, and health metrics must render with tabular figures (font-mono or tabular-nums) to prevent optical jitter and visual misalignment in dense schedules.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Content cards, data tables, and input fields never carry default box shadows. Structural boundaries are achieved exclusively via background separation and hairline border strokes.

dos: Do format all consultation fees with currency denomination (e.g., ৳ 1,200 BDT) and tabular figures.
Do use explicit state pills (SCHEDULED, INPROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELED) with consistent semantic colors across all screens.
Do maintain a strict 4.5:1 text-to-background contrast ratio for all clinical data and form labels.
Do reserve Assist Violet exclusively for features touching the Medix AI clinical assistant.
donts: Don't use bounce or elastic easing for loading spinners, drawers, or dialogs; use smooth exponential ease-out curves.
Don't apply thick colored side-tab borders on content cards (e.g. border-l-4).
Don't use saturated red for non-destructive actions; red is strictly reserved for failed payments, cancellations, and clinical allergies.
Don't fabricate artificial testimonials or false medical guarantees.
